tasks.title: Pure novelty and duplication classifier classify_novelty() against prior-submission corpus
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/novelty_gate.py exists and exports classify_novelty(finding: dict, known_corpus: list) -> str.
Returns 'NOVEL', 'POSSIBLE_DUP', or 'CONFIRMED_DUP' based on the specified rules, with empty corpus resulting in 'NOVEL'.
CONFIRMED_DUP is returned if any corpus entry matches the finding on cwe, file, and normalized title.
POSSIBLE_DUP is returned if no CONFIRMED_DUP matches but a similar title match exists OR (same cwe AND same file).
Title normalization lowercases, strips outer whitespace, and collapses internal whitespace sequences into a single space, performing substring match in either direction for similarity.
Module is stdlib-only, deterministic, and performs no I/O, database, network, LLM, wall-clock, or subprocess calls.

spec.objective: Implement a pure, stdlib+ngv2-only, deterministic novelty and duplication classifier that ports the legacy novelty_checker.py logic to decide if a finding is NOVEL, a POSSIBLE_DUP, or a CONFIRMED_DUP.
functional_requirements: Expose classify_novelty(finding: dict, known_corpus: list) -> str which is a pure and deterministic function.
Extract 'title', 'cwe', and 'file' fields from finding (must carry at least these keys).
Iterate through each entry in known_corpus (each entry being a dict containing 'title', 'cwe', and 'file').
Normalize titles by lowercasing, stripping leading/trailing whitespace, and collapsing all internal whitespace sequences to a single space.

Perform title matching: for CONFIRMED_DUP, check if normalized titles are exactly equal. For POSSIBLE_DUP, check if normalized finding title is a substring of normalized corpus entry title, or vice-versa.
Match file-locus by checking if the finding's 'file' value is equal to the corpus entry's 'file' value.

Apply the decision rule: CONFIRMED_DUP iff some corpus entry has the same cwe AND same file AND equal normalized title. Else POSSIBLE_DUP iff some corpus entry has a similar title OR (same cwe AND same file). Else NOVEL.
If the corpus is empty, immediately return 'NOVEL'.
Resolve multiple matching entries deterministically: if any entry matches CONFIRMED_DUP, the verdict must be 'CONFIRMED_DUP' (strongest match wins).
Ensure exception-safety: handle missing keys, None values, or wrong types in finding or known_corpus entries gracefully without raising exceptions.
spec.interfaces: exposes `classify_novelty(finding: dict, known_corpus: list) -> str` returning 'NOVEL'|'POSSIBLE_DUP'|'CONFIRMED_DUP'.
edge_cases: Whitespace normalization: handles multiple consecutive spaces, tabs, and newlines by collapsing them to a single space, and strips leading/trailing whitespaces.
Substring match in either direction: checks normalized_finding_title in normalized_corpus_title OR normalized_corpus_title in normalized_finding_title.
Finding or corpus entries with extra fields are handled gracefully without exceptions.
Exact cwe and file-locus comparison matches case-sensitively (or handles mismatching formats gracefully).
non_goals: Do not implement real database connections, network requests, platform/advisory API calls, embeddings, or fuzzy ML similarity.
Do not perform the FSM transition or the operator-override routing (handled by wiring brief).
No subprocess, LLM, wall-clock, or randomness.
spec.implementation_notes:
Keep the module free of any I/O or import beyond the Python standard library. Define a helper function for title normalization to collapse and strip whitespaces. Evaluate CONFIRMED_DUP first or track if any entry qualifies for it to ensure the strongest match wins over POSSIBLE_DUP. Use the credential-naming constraint (avoid variables named with 'password', 'secret', or 'key').

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Dictionaries representing findings and corpus entries with varying combinations of 'title', 'cwe', 'file', and extra fields, along with empty and mock inputs.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation covers pure classification logic and whitespace normalization; test budget is for verifying edge cases and exception safety.
